title: Gemmini (ucb-bar/gemmini) -- LeanGemmini on rocket-chip DefaultConfig
_note: Gemmini's LeanGemmini systolic-array accelerator -- the Mesh of PEs with its
delay registers, the scratchpad and accumulator memories with their scaling
pipelines, the DMA, the TLB, the reservation station, the loop-matmul
unrollers and the transposer -- attached as a RoCC accelerator to
rocket-chip's DefaultConfig SoC and emitted by firtool as one SystemVerilog
file per module, the same shape as the rocket-chip and boom families.
Why generation is not simply `mill` or `sbt` in the Gemmini checkout.
Gemmini is a Chisel LIBRARY with no elaboration target, normally built inside
chipyard, and four things stand between the checkout and a row -- all
measured on 2026-10-27 and all recorded in test/ext_ip/gemmini_setup.sh:
* It needs rocket-chip on the classpath, so it is compiled as an extra
module APPENDED to the rocket-chip checkout's build.sc, which this family
clones alongside and the rocket-chip family already elaborates (the same
route as boom_setup.sh).  mill, firtool 1.162.0 and dtc come from
rocket_setup.sh.
* Gemmini's build.sbt pins chisel3 3.6.0 against that checkout's 6.7.0, and
it costs NOTHING: a bare compile raises not one Chisel-version error.
* All 38 errors of that bare compile are TWO symbols from FireSim's
annotation library, midas.targetutils.PerfCounter and .SynthesizePrintf,
which live in firesim and reach Gemmini only through chipyard.  Both are
pure instrumentation for FPGA-accelerated simulation and carry no
hardware, so gemmini_harness/midas/targetutils/ shims them -- a no-op
counter and the plain Printable the printf needs.
* No Gemmini config can be instantiated by the generator: every accelerator
mixin is `class LeanGemminiConfig[T <: Data : Arithmetic, U, V](
gemminiConfig: ... = GemminiConfigs.leanConfig)` -- type parameters with a
context bound AND a defaulted argument -- while the generator reflects on
each --config.  gemmini_harness/gemminisweep/ owns the no-arg wrappers
over rocket-chip's DefaultConfig, with the system bus widened to 128 bits
exactly as chipyard's own GemminiRocketConfig does (the default 16x16
8-bit array moves 16 bytes a beat and the 8-byte default bus cannot carry
it).
One firtool trap: Chisel stamps an EnumComponentAnnotation on every
enum-typed signal purely so waveform tooling can name the enumerators, and
where such a signal is a field of a MEMORY PORT -- Gemmini's
Queue6_TagWithIdAndTotalRows, whose entries hold a NormCmd enum -- firtool
cannot resolve the target and HARD-ERRORS even under
--disable-annotation-unknown.  The setup script drops exactly those (16 of
1006 annotations, both the `io_deq_bits_MPORT` read-port and the bare
`MPORT` write-port spellings) and leaves DontTouch / BlackBoxInline /
Inline / DecodeTable untouched, so the emitted RTL is unchanged.
always_srcs: the two Verilog blackboxes the generated modules instantiate
(plusarg_reader, EICG_wrapper) ship in rocket-chip's src/main/resources/vsrc,
not in the firtool output.  Excluded, as in the rocket-chip and boom
families: the TestHarness and its simulation-only models, the TLMonitor
assertion checkers, and the TestHarness-scale AXI backing memory.
First local sweep 2026-10-27 (384 rows, MEM_LIMIT_KB=7000000 as the nightly
uses): 340 / 384 comparable proven, 383 / 384 elaborate, 380 co-sim PASS,
0 undriven on every row that elaborated, and ZERO `differs` rows and ZERO
co-simulated divergences -- the cleanest first sweep of any family in this
campaign.  7.1 h of row time over six shards.
Open: 43 rows exhaust the SAT budget (27 timeout, 16 over the memory cap),
each with a clean co-simulation -- the systolic-array rows (Mesh,
MeshWithDelays), the scratchpad / accumulator memories and the wide
TileLink crossbars; and ExampleRocketSystem, the whole-SoC row, cannot
elaborate under the 7 GB cap at all (a 43 MB source closure, aborting in
Surelog), the same whole-core class as BlackParrot and boom's four.
